text_en: The reporter learned that the regulator summarized the current shareholding structure of the securities industry in the latest issue of "Communication." As of August 2026, among 104 securities firms, 71 were state-owned, accounting for 68.3%, including 23 controlled by central state-owned enterprises and 48 controlled by local governments; 16 were foreign-funded securities firms, accounting for 15.4%; 11 were private securities firms, accounting for 10.5%; and 6 were mixed-ownership securities firms, accounting for 5.7%. A pattern dominated by state-owned capital with orderly participation by various types of capital is the situation of the shareholding structure of domestic securities firms. It is worth noting that the concentration of different types of securities firms shows an obvious gradient. The largest shareholders of foreign-funded and private institutions hold relatively high average stakes, at 77.4% and 71.9% respectively. The former mostly adopts a wholly-owned or absolute controlling model by the parent company, while the latter has higher shareholdings by founding shareholders and industrial capital.
